import {Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard} from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

You want this when "why did that component update?" takes more than one guess.
The Timeline panel records Lit lifecycle, render, mouse, and keyboard events on
a layered stream you can scrub, and the Components tab shows the live element
tree with each element's reactive state.

The Timeline panel is a **Vue DevTools–style** event recorder for Lit components,
served as a panel inside [Vite DevTools](https://devtools.vite.dev) (`@vitejs/devtools`).

## Enable it

```ts
import {litPlugin} from '@oddsquad/vite-plugin-lit';
import {DevTools} from '@vitejs/devtools';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    litPlugin({timeline: true}),
    DevTools(), // required: provides the DevTools panel host
  ],
});
```

Or with the env var (`.env.local`):

```
LIT_PLUGIN_TIMELINE=true
```

<Aside type="caution" title="Experimental">
  `timeline` defaults to `false` while the panel is experimental, and it is
  dev-only — nothing about it reaches a production build.
</Aside>

## Layers

| Layer         | What it captures                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Lit Lifecycle | `connectedCallback`, `performUpdate`, `willUpdate`, `update`, `updated`, `firstUpdated`, `disconnectedCallback` — with per-phase duration bars and changed-property keys |
| Lit Render    | `begin/end render` from Lit's built-in `lit-debug` events                                                                                                                |
| Mouse         | `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `click`, `dblclick`                                                                                                                              |
| Keyboard      | `keydown`, `keyup`                                                                                                                                                       |

Click any event row to see the element tag name, stable instance id, source
file (click it to open in your editor), and raw event data. The element row also has an **inspect** link that opens the
[Components](#components) tab on that element (they share the same instance id).

Layer toggles are remembered between sessions (localStorage).

## Components

The **Components** tab shows a live, hierarchical tree of the Lit elements on
the page (descending through shadow roots) and a details pane for the selected
one: its reactive properties and internal `@state`, current attributes, update
flags (`updated` / `update pending` / `shadow root`), and a source link that
opens the component in your editor. The details refresh in place as the selected
element updates.

:::note[How the panel opens files]
Both source links prefer
[`@devframes/service-open`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@devframes/service-open),
the shared open-in-editor service Vite DevTools installs on its host. It only
opens files under the workspace root, resolving symlinks before it decides.
When it is not there — or it refuses the path, which happens for a source
outside the workspace root — the panel falls back to the plugin's own
`/__lit-open-in-editor` endpoint, which trusts everything Vite itself serves
(`server.fs.allow`) and is also the only path the in-page
[source overlay](/vite-plugin-lit/guides/source-overlay/) uses. Either way the
editor is picked by `launch-editor`, so you land on the same file and line.
:::

Hovering a row outlines that element in the page. When the panel is docked
inside the app's own window it draws the outline by talking to the page
directly, with no round trip through the dev server; opened as its own tab
there is no page to talk to, so it falls back to the server route. Either way
the outline is the same.

The tree refreshes on demand (the **Refresh** button) and whenever you pick an
element. For continuous updates, toggle **Live** — an opt-in `MutationObserver`
in the page (off by default, remembered per browser) that re-pushes the tree as
the component hierarchy changes, including inside shadow roots.

To pick an element by pointing at it on the page, use the **Pick** button in the
tab, or the `Ctrl+Shift+E` shortcut (also in the DevTools command palette as
_Inspect Lit Element_). This reuses the source-overlay picker, so it requires
[`sourceOverlay`](/vite-plugin-lit/guides/source-overlay/) to be enabled — but
unlike `Ctrl+Shift+S` (which opens the element in your editor), a pick selects
the element in the Components tree.

## Settings

The **Settings** tab shows the plugin's resolved configuration — `options` on
top of `LIT_PLUGIN_*` env vars on top of the defaults — and lets you override
the HMR behaviour and the source-overlay editor live, without restarting the
dev server or editing `vite.config.ts`. **Reset** drops the overrides and puts
the resolved values back. A setting whose feature is disabled at config time
stays read-only: its runtime was never injected into the page.

These overrides, and the panel's own light/dark preference, persist
per-developer through devframe's settings store — under Vite DevTools that is
`~/.vite/devtools/settings/lit.json`. They follow you to another browser on
the same machine, and survive clearing site data or restarting the dev server.
Nothing is written into the repository, so no `.gitignore` entry is needed —
and nothing is shared with teammates. Project-wide defaults belong in
`litPlugin({...})`, which is committed on purpose.

`localStorage` is still written, and still matters: the inspected page reads
the overrides synchronously as its modules initialise, before any connection
to DevTools exists, so it cannot wait on the settings store. Treat it as a
per-browser cache that the panel refills from the durable copy on its first
connection. The practical consequence: in a browser that has never opened the
panel for this project, the page starts with the resolved config and picks the
overrides up once you open the panel.

## Link to a view

The panel is addressable. Opened on its own (or from an exported snapshot), it
reads its position from the URL hash and keeps it up to date as you click, so
copying the address bar gives a link that reopens the same view:

```
#tab=components&component=7
```

`tab` is `timeline`, `components` or `settings`; `component` is the element id
shown in the Components tree. The hash, not the query string — the query is
where the DevTools handshake token lives, and that must not travel in a link
you paste into an issue.

Inside Vite DevTools the panel is an iframe whose address nobody reads, so
links arrive over RPC instead. Anything with a DevTools client can ask the hub
to bring this panel forward on a specific element:

```ts
await rpc.call('hub:docks:activate', {
  dockId: 'lit',
  params: {tab: 'components', componentId: 7},
});
```

This is also how picking an element in the page lands you on it: the plugin
activates its own dock with the picked id attached.

## Export a session

**Export snapshot** in the Timeline tab freezes the current session — the
recorded events, the component tree, the details of everything you opened, and
any HMR incompatibilities — into a self-contained directory. The dev server
writes it; the panel just asks.

The result is a static site: open `index.html` from any file server and the
panel renders the recording with no dev server, no checkout of the app, and no
reproduction steps. Zip it onto a bug report and the person reading it sees
what actually happened instead of a description of it.

The frozen panel is read-only by construction. Recording, picking and tree
refresh are hidden, because there is no page behind it to command.

Two limits worth knowing when you record something to report:

- Only components you actually opened have their details baked. Details are
  read from live DOM, so there is nothing to freeze for a component nobody
  inspected — click through the ones that matter before exporting.
- The timeline keeps its most recent events, not all of them. A long session
  exports its tail.

`lit-devtools build` does **not** produce one of these: a fresh CLI process has
no session to freeze. Export from the running server that recorded it.

## Ask a coding agent

The panel is a [devframe](https://devfra.me), so the same data it renders is
exposed to coding agents over MCP. Vite DevTools mounts the server at
`/__devtools/__mcp` on the dev server, and six tools appear there:

| Tool                        | Answers                                                               |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lit_get-meta`              | Plugin version, available timeline layers, resolved settings.         |
| `lit_list-components`       | The live element tree, with each component's source file and line.    |
| `lit_component-details`     | Reactive properties, attributes, and update flags for one element id. |
| `lit_recent-events`         | Recent lifecycle/render/input events, filterable by element or layer. |
| `lit_hmr-incompatibilities` | Components the plugin could not hot-patch in place, and why.          |
| `lit_set-recording`         | Starts or stops timeline recording. The only tool that changes state. |

Five of the six only read. The exception is `lit_set-recording`, which exists
because `lit_recent-events` is a dead end while recording is off — an agent
that can read the timeline but not start it can only hand the question back to
you. Recording is a shared toggle, so an agent turning it on also changes what
you see in an open panel. Everything else that changes the page — the layer
toggles and the element picker — stays panel-only.

Point your agent at the dev server's `/__devtools/__mcp` endpoint and it can
answer "what's on this page, what state is it in, and why did it re-render?"
against the running app instead of guessing from source.

<Aside type="caution" title="Dev servers are not public">
  The MCP endpoint has the same trust model as the rest of DevTools: it binds to
  localhost and expects a local developer. Do not expose a dev server with
  DevTools enabled to a network you do not control.
</Aside>
